messages.subject: [statnet_help] uniform homophily?
messages.body_plain:
Dear list,

I have one (probably dumb) question about the nodematch() term. I saw analyses interpreted sometimes as "homophily", sometime as "uniform homophily" or "differential homophily". I know that when diff=T, it is testing differential homophily; but when diff=F, is it testing uniform homophily or some other kind of homophily?

I know the help page says "nodematch(attrname, diff=FALSE, keep=NULL) (binary), nodematch(attrname, diff=FALSE, keep=NULL, form="sum") (valued) a.k.a. match
Uniform homophily and differential homophily: The attrname argument is a character vector giving one or more names of attributes in the network's vertex attribute list. When diff=FALSE, this term adds one network statistic to the model, which counts the number of edges (i,j) for which attrname(i)==attrname(j)." 

I just want to be clear about this issue. Could you give me some advice please? Thank you very much.

Best regards,



ya

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Degree assortativity parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,
I think the ergm term "degcor" may be what you're looking for.  So if 
you just want to calculate it for an observed network (not conduct 
inference about it), the syntax would be:

summary(mynetwork~degcor)

You can see more info at help("ergm-terms") and scrolling down to degcor.

HTH,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Degree assortativity parameter
messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

As far as I now, we don't have a directed version of it available. I think this is in part because we haven't seen demand for it before, and because 
there are multiple different ways to consider measures like this for directed networks (correlation in in-degree, out-degree, total degree, head's 
in-degree with tail's out-degree, etc.) So your quickest optionis to use igraph or another program, if it has the statistic you want. Alternately, if 
you wish to be able to conduct statistical inference on your model with the ergm framework, then you can code up the statistic yourself with help from 
the ergm.userterms package and instructions here: http://www.jstatsoft.org/v52/i02

Yours,
Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] egocentric data - ERGM
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vanesse,

On Fri, 5 Dec 2014, vanesse labeyrie wrote:

> Dear all,
> 
> I have seen on the program of Sunbelt 2015 that you are going to release a package for egocentric data ERGM (ergm.ego),
> and I would like to know when do you plan to release it.

Most likely sometime in May 2015, with the general update of statnet. 
Note that you can already perform the analyses using existing tools (see 
the last sections of the ergm tutorial).  What ergm.ego will do is provide 
a set of utilities to facilitate this, and proper statistical inference.

> My second question is whether it will be possible to simulate a complete model from an ERGM with parameters associated
> with the following observed? statistics:? GWESP, GWDSP, GWdegree, homophily and geographical distance

Observing the triads needed to estimate the gw*sp terms requires 
collecting the alter-alter tie matrix data.  So if that's what you have, 
right?  Currently the package does not include these terms, as we've 
focused on the minimal egocentric design, but we can code those up between 
now and the release date.  I'll check with Pavel Krivitsky (the package 
developer) about geographical distance.

best,
mm

> Vanesse

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tom,

Here is some code to do it.  Notice that I altered your example so that 
there are only "" (zero length string) not also " " (a single space).


data<-matrix(c("a", "b", "a", "c", "a", "d", "b", "a", "b" , "c", "b", 
"b", "d", "e", "c", "", "d", "a","d", "b", "d", "e", "f", "", "g", 
""),13,2,byrow=TRUE)


Here is a quick and dirty way via a vertex deletion:

data_net2<-as.network(data,directed=FALSE)
data_net2<-delete.vertices(data_net2,which(network.vertex.names(data_net2)==''))
plot(data2_net,displaylabels=TRUE)



Here is a much longer (and perhaps more flexible?) way to do it 
step-by-step with no deletion


#figure unique labels/non-numeric ids for vertices
ids<-unique(as.vector(data))

# remove the blank id and sort
ids<-sort(ids[ids!=''])

# remove the rows in the matrix that have ""
data<-data[data[,2]!="",]

# replace the labels with numeric indices
data[,1]<-match(data[,1],ids)
data[,2]<-match(data[,2],ids)

# initialize the network with the right number of vertices
data_net<-network.initialize(length(ids),directed=FALSE)

# set the vertex names
network.vertex.names(data_net)<-ids

# use the edgelist constructor load edges into the network
data_net<-network.edgelist(data,data_net)

plot(data_net,displaylabels=TRUE)


In your example, "c" wasn't actually an isolate, but id was missing the 
other half of its dyad

best,

messages.subject: [statnet_help] absdiff / nodematch interaction
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am trying to model a series of directed, valued, one-mode networks.
The nodes are members of European parliaments, and edges are bill
cosponsorships.

All nodes carry the following attributes:

- a leftwing/rightwing score (0-10)
- a government/opposition dummy (0/1)

Using the `ergm` package, I am interested in modelling the effect of
leftwing/rightwing ideology within each possible type of dyads, in
order to ask:

  Is the absolute difference in leftwing/rightwing ideology
significant to predict edge formation when ...

  - ... both nodes are from the government majority?
  - ... both nodes are from opposition parties?
  - ... the nodes are asymmetric (gov/opp or opp/gov)?

Unfortunately, I could not figure out a way to code this into a proper
ERGM equation so far. As far as I understand, the net effects are:

  - `absdiff("score")` for the absolute difference in leftwing/rightwing
  - `nodematch("dummy", diff = TRUE)` for the differential homophily term

... but how do I code the interaction?

Any help would be very appreciated.

Best regards,

Fran?ois

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Comparing coefficients in same model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Julija,

I don't know if such a comprehensive approach is actually needed in your 
case, but Desmarais and Cranmer proposed a unified approach to the 
micro-level interpretation of ERGMs at the tie-, dyad- and block level:

Desmarais, Bruce A. and Skyler J. Cranmer (2012): Micro-Level 
Interpretation of Exponential Random Graph Models with Application to 
Estuary Networks. The Policy Studies Journal 40(3): 402-434.

With this approach, you can also answer more complicated questions, such as:
- What is the probability of a tie between nodes i and j if j has three 
other incoming ties (given the rest of the network and the model)?
- How much more (or less) likely is a tie in a dyad when a specific 
coefficient is set to zero?
- How likely is an edge from i to j if the reciprocal edge (ji) exists 
(vs. does not exist)?
- What is the probability that i is tied to j but not to k and l?
etc.

These questions can be answered for specific nodes or dyads (using the 
node index or the vertex name), but one can also use sampling to 
generalize this to all nodes or dyads or specific subsets of them.

If you have dichotomous covariates, you could, for example, sample among 
dyads where one covariate exclusively holds, then sample again from 
dyads where the other covariate exclusively holds, then do the same 
thing again for dyads where both covariates hold, and compare the tie 
probabilities of those groups and compute confidence intervals for each 
of them. Or you could compute the tie probabilities for each level of an 
ordinal covariate and look at the shape of the association, and compare 
this for several covariates.

While their paper comes with some companion R code, the code is a little 
buggy and outdated. Meanwhile, I have rewritten their original code and 
included it in the xergm package as a function called "interpret". The 
help page for that function contains some examples on micro-level 
interpretation. Note that the xergm package is not part of the statnet 
suite of packages; it just provides some support functions for the ergm 
package and other extensions.

Best,
Philip

messages.body_plain:
Alex,

If I'm understanding you correctly, you want to see the coefficient table,
but not the entire summary of the ergm object. If that's the case, this
should do the trick:

lapply(nets, function(x) {summary(x)$coef})

If you want to save these results, just point this code to a new object:

ergm.summaries <- lapply(nets, function(x) {summary(x)$coef})

HTH,

Matt

messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael,

Old versions of R packages are archived on CRAN. For example for
package 'ergm' they are here
http://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/ergm/

In principle, when you open package page on CRAN (like this for ergm
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/ergm/index.html) there should
be a link "old sources" that should direct to a page with older
versions of that particular package.

Do mind that these are package sources. If you work on Windows you
will have to install additional software to install these old package
versions. For more info see e.g. here:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4739837/how-do-i-install-an-r-package-from-the-source-tarball-on-windows


hth,

Michal

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ergm for weighted graphs
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
I have a weighted network which is made of countries and the drug  
exchanges (estimated quantity) among them, and I would like to use an ergm  
to analyse it. I see from the workshop materials of the 2014 Sunbelt that  
ergms for valued ties has been added in the list of additional  
functionalities. I have two questions about this:
- Is there an updated tutorial on ergms for weighted graphs? (Or should I  
refer to the 2013 Sunbelt tutorial on valued networks? And, if so, is  
there any update since then?)
- Do I need discrete data in my weighted network to run the ergm?
Thank you in advance!
All the best,
Giulia
